contexts.text: Everyone supposes his own dogma to be true, and thence receives a conscience... For many are regenerated by the Lord, from every dogma whatever... AC 2053:2. AC 8521:2.
Besides other things which are dogmatic, and which in like manner are known from charity alone.
The doctrinal things and dogmas of faith are not faith, but are of faith...
The Ancient Church... was turned partly into... a certain dogmatic affair separate from charity.
Preface. Each confirms his own dogma from the literal sense of the Word. AC 3427:3. AC 6222:2. AC 6222.
Such do not want to see the truth which is in the Word; but they remain obstinately in their own dogma. AC 4368:2.
Under Doctrine, see this reference.
Range through it in trading, and possess ye in it = that the dogmas from a general principle would agree together. AC 4479:end.

That faith is now separated from charity is evident, for Churches separate themselves according to their dogmas, and he who believes otherwise than as dogma teaches is cast out from their communion and defamed...
It is believed to be sufficient to know the dogmas of the faith which belong to the Church in which he has been born, and to confirm them in various ways.
As may be evident from the fact, that each remains in the dogma in which he was born.
Under Confirm, see these references. NJHD 257:4.
The princes of the sea = the primary scientifics, which are called dogmas.
In agreement with the good dogmas of their religion...
Such a dogma follows of necessity... DLord 18:2.
The Angels utterly reject this dogma, that the understanding must be under obedience to faith... Thus this dogmatic thing recedes.
With these, ignorance is the defence of dogmas.
This takes place only when Spirits bring in something dogmatic of religion, which is never done by any good Spirit, still less by any Angel.
They then enter the cells... where are those who confirm their dogmatic things from the Word...
As in the New Church this dogma is rejected, that the understanding is to be kept under obedience to faith...
The disagreements between the dogmas of the present Church and those of the New Church.
Its dogmas only enter the memory...
The dogmas of the present Church can be learned only with great difficulty...
The opening and rejection of the dogmas of the faith of the present Church, and the revelation and reception of the dogmas of the faith of the New Church. Signified.

The reason the falsities of the dogmas of the faith of the present Church are to be opened, before the Truths of the dogmas of the New Church are revealed and received, is that they do not agree in a single point or particle; for the dogmas of the present Church are founded upon a faith in which it is not known whether there is any essential of the Church or not.
Quite the contrary is the case with the dogmas or doctrinal things of the New Church; these are all essential things...

All Protestants... after they have been instructed in dogmatic things by Luther, etc., these dogmatic things do not speak of themselves through them, but they speak of themselves from the dogmatic things: every dogma may also be expounded in a thousand ways...
The faith of every Church is like a seed from which all its dogmas spring.
To confirm some dogma of the Church...
From the wisdom of the Ancients there flowed forth this dogma, that the universe and everything in it have relation to good and truth...
It was necessary to proclaim the dogma that the understanding is to be kept under obedience to faith.
It was necessary first to put forth decisions and dogmas concerning God and the Divine Trinity; and afterwards to establish decisions and dogmas concerning faith and charity, etc.
Afterwards, he draws the doctrinal things of faith and charity from parents, etc.; and, when he becomes capable of judging for himself, from the Word and from dogmatic books...
This dogmatic tenet is as a door to the doctrine of charity.
Is not this according to the dogma of our people?
It is exceedingly dangerous to enter with the understanding into dogmas of faith which have been forged from our own intelligence... and still more to confirm them from the Word...
The dogmatic teachers of the Christian religion have stopped up their ears as with wax...
From the time Luther first entered the Spiritual World, he was a most vehement propagator and defender of his dogmas...
Calvin... concluded all the dogmas of his faith from his own intelligence, and not from the Word.
On those who are called learned... because they can confirm their own dogma.
As to this dogmatic saying that the tree lies where it falls...
I. Let a man read the Word every day, one chapter or two, and learn from a teacher and from preachings the dogmas of his religion...
When any received dogma is assumed as the truth itself...
Trinity. 8. 2. After confirmation, a man does not see anything but that his dogmas are true, although they are falsities.
